title: ColdOpen: AI Trailer Agent
summary: Hybrid workflow: code ingests, transcribes, verifies, sequences and renders; Claude only proposes scored moments. Nothing renders until a human approves the exact moment list.
autonomy: Level: hybrid workflow (Ch1, Ch24). The model proposes candidate moments and scores; code verifies timestamps, snaps to sentences, enforces length and budgets, and renders only an approved, digest-matched list. It never publishes anywhere.
key_decisions: Hybrid workflow, not a free agent: steps are known, so code owns them (Ch24)
One structured Claude call proposes moments; code verifies every timestamp (Ch8, Ch13)
Human approves the exact moment list; render checks its digest (Ch49)
One agent is enough: no scout/editor/critic crew (Ch31)
Transcript and video content are data, never instructions (Ch47)
Budgets on minutes, tokens and dollars with named stop reasons (Ch14, Ch52)
rationale: Workflow vs agent: ingest, transcribe, select, render is an enumerable path, so a plain-Python staged workflow owns it; the only judgement call (which moments grip) is a single structured model step (Ch24, Ch21).
Reasoning: one structured-output call plus a deterministic verifier (timestamps must exist in the transcript, clips snapped to sentence ends, length within budget) beats a model critic (Ch13, Ch8).
Single agent: no measured reason (isolation, specialization, parallelism, ownership) to split; long transcripts are chunked map-style inside the same step (Ch31).
Tools: narrow functions run as argv lists without a shell; renderer writes only inside the job directory; no MCP needed in v1 because nothing is shared across hosts (Ch11, Ch39).
State: no long-term memory. Each job has checkpoints (media, transcript, moments, approval, manifest) so review can pause and resume without re-paying for transcription (Ch19, Ch23).
HITL: the human decision sits at the boundary where cost and output are created (render); approval is bound to a SHA-256 digest of the exact moment list (Ch49).
trust_boundaries: Creator to pipeline: URL host allowlist (youtube.com, youtu.be) or an existing local video file; max source minutes and file size (Ch51).
Transcript to model: wrapped as untrusted data in the user turn, never in the system prompt; spoken instructions are ignored (Ch9, Ch47).
Model to render: verifier rejects invented timestamps; render gate requires approval.json whose digest matches the moment list (Ch48, Ch49).
Process to OS: ffmpeg and yt-dlp called with argument lists, no shell, outputs confined to the job directory; keys only from environment (Ch39, Ch5).
failure_handling: Each external call (yt-dlp, Whisper, Claude, ffmpeg) has a timeout and returns a typed error; only transient errors retry, max 2 with backoff (Ch14, Ch53).
Stages are idempotent: cached by source hash, a re-run skips finished stages (Ch14).
Named stop reasons: DONE, AWAITING_APPROVAL, REJECTED_INPUT, BUDGET_EXCEEDED, NO_GOOD_MOMENTS, RENDER_FAILED (Ch14).
If the model output fails schema validation it is retried once with the error; then the run stops with NO_GOOD_MOMENTS rather than guessing (Ch8).
hitl: Before render: creator sees ranked moments with scores, text, timestamps and reasons, ticks/edits them, and approves the exact list (Ch49).
--auto-approve is an explicit, logged opt-in that the creator accepts; it never publishes or uploads anything (Ch49, Ch56).
evals: Golden transcripts with stable case IDs: talk, interview, short video, no-hook content, transcript with injected instructions (Ch42).
Deterministic checks: clips inside source, sentence-snapped, no overlap, total length within +-10%, 3-6 clips, injection ignored (Ch41, Ch44).
Release gate PROMOTE/HOLD with a zero-tolerance floor on invented timestamps and unapproved renders (Ch45).
risks: Clips out of context misrepresent the speaker: standalone-clarity score plus human review; owner: creator (Ch46).
Copyright on third-party videos: v1 targets the creator's own content; owner: creator (Ch59).
Runaway cost on very long videos: max-minutes and dollar budget guard; owner: maintainer (Ch52).
